questions.q: What is true about certification by default, before a tenant admin changes anything?
options: It's off for the whole organization until an admin enables it
It's on for every user automatically
It only applies to datasets created before 2020
It requires a separate Power BI Premium license
questions.explain: Certification is disabled tenant-wide by default — an admin has to deliberately turn it on and decide who gets to use it.

questions.q: What does the tenant-level certification setting actually control?
options: How often datasets automatically refresh
Who is allowed to certify content — the whole org, specific security groups, or delegated domain admins
Which visuals are available in Power BI Desktop
The color of the Certified badge
questions.explain: This setting answers the key governance question: who's allowed to certify? It can be scoped to everyone, specific security groups, or delegated to domain admins.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what should be true about a dataset before it's certified?
options: It should have a known owner, a documented refresh schedule, and reviewed accuracy against written criteria
It should have at least 100 reports connected to it
It should never have been edited by more than one person
It should be stored in a Premium-capacity workspace only
questions.explain: A badge only means something if it's backed by a real standard: a known owner, a documented refresh schedule, and accuracy reviewed against written criteria.

questions.q: What does Power BI itself actually enforce when someone certifies a dataset?
options: That the data has zero errors
That the dataset has been reviewed by at least three people
Only that the user clicking Certified actually holds certifier rights — the review process itself happens outside the tool
That the refresh schedule runs nightly
questions.explain: Power BI enforces who is allowed to apply the badge. Whether a real review actually happened first is a process the organization has to enforce outside the tool.

questions.q: Does certification apply only to datasets?
options: Yes, certification is exclusive to datasets and cannot be applied to anything else
No — published apps carry their own Endorse option, and the same certification concept applies there too
No, certification only applies to reports, never datasets
Yes, but only in Power BI Premium
questions.explain: Published apps have their own Endorse option in their settings — the same certification concept (and the same two questions: criteria met, and permission held) extends beyond just datasets.
